questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I've been living in Paris since january 2022, it was important for me to have the oppertunity to stay in the city, but at the same time not compromise with my studies

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find information. Most of the information about the new semester was sent by email.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The coordinator i was assigned was always available to help. However, at the meeting with all the new exchange students, there weren't left much time for questions and the coordinators seemed busy to move on.

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It can be very difficult and expensive to find housing in Paris on your own, the best thing is to go there a month in advance to look for a place to stay. Furthermore it can be difficult to find an apartment for only 6 months, but it is doable.

Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: All you had to do was to fill out a paper with the course codes. These were given to us on pieces of paper, if the course wasn't on the paper, it wasn't available

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The coordinator was there to tell you if you had made a mistake, but everything was very clear to begin with

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull, I got all the classes I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you want a class that is not among the ones the university offer, ask again, it might be possible after all

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very sad to find out that I was only allowed to take seminars as a master student, I was told this rather late in the process. For my particular courses it meant that I had to do 10-15 pages of what is called "mini-mémoire" in each of my 5 courses, which in totalt made up 60 pages to write during the time I was also taking my classes, as most of the mini-mémoires were due before the holidays. While it is possible to follow 5 courses and write 60 pages on 5 different subjects, I do not recommend it, and personally I would have liked to be informed about the exam method in advance. It is important to point out that this is exam method does not apply to all seminars, and that French students normally have 2 seminars, where as a master exchange student you are forced to have 5-6 seminars, which with different exam methods is fine, but I cannot recommend only chosing courses with mini-mémoire as the final.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level was very different depending on the class, I had a gender studies course that had its main focus on student presentations, but for the most part it was the professor who presented the subjects. The academic level was usually appropriate

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Because I only had seminars, it was mostly the professor talking and presenting a subject, and the professor would at the end of a class ask if the students had questions for the last 5 min. 
There were a lot of homework in some of the courses, but only for the literature courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
M1FR470A : Pourquoi la littérature ? les écrivains disent le littéraire en francophonie
M1FR470B : La fabrique d'auteur: mises en scène de l'écrivain francophone 
M1FR430A : Rhétorique, poétique, genres littéraires à l'époque moderne 
M1FR482C : Identités troublées : pensée queer et littérature
M1FR433A : Littérature et histoire des idées à l'âge classique Écrire sur l'art à l'âge classique

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The rhétorique course was great in many ways, it was fun to learn how to analyse texts which were written B.C, and to use rhetorical analysis methods from Cicéron, Aristote and Ferrazzi. Personally I have never been taught in rhetorics on this level, but the professor was very passionate and very likable.
Both of the courses in francophonie was taught by the same professor, they were very informative and very interresting courses, the literature we had to read was very well chosen. Furthermore, francophonie and the francophone literature is generally a very important subject, and it only gets better with a passionate professor.
I can also recommend the course : Littérature et histoire des idées à l'âge classique Écrire sur l'art à l'âge classique. The course is heavy on the historical perspective on writings of art, but the professor made the teaching very lively and fun to participate in.

questions.answer: Take your time to go to the different areas of the city, there are great spots all over the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was somewhat easy, I had already been on one exchange in Normandie, Caen, so I wasn't chocked by anything, however, Paris is quite different from Normandy but it is quick to adjust to the cultural differences

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The most important part is not to be scared to talk to them, French students aren't used to be making friends at the university, but don't hesitate to go over to them in the break, before or after class, you might get yourself invited to a apéro

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the professors are (usually) always right and that it is normal for both students and professors to be late

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That people are very polite on the street and in the metro. I enjoy that it is expected to say hello when you walk into any type of shop. I like how common it is to meet up with your friends for just one drink before dinner. The general appriciation of art, food and their own culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
When authorities tell you no, it doesn't always mean it isn't a possibility (within reason).
Don't be scared to ask questions, neither to the professors or the other students, chances are the other students are just as lost as you feel.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you don't financially need to have a student job while you're here, don't get one, while it is a good way to improve your french and meet new people, it is a lot to get accostumed to, and you might not have as much free time as you think.
